name: EscapeBench
description: An agent benchmark built around room escape game environments that test creative reasoning, unconventional tool use, and iterative problem-solving. Unlike goal-directed agent benchmarks, EscapeBench requires lateral thinking — using objects in unexpected ways, discovering hidden mechanisms, and reasoning under uncertainty without clear subgoal decomposition. Current LLMs achieve only 15% average progress without hints.
evaluation_method: progress rate (% of escape steps completed); binary task success rate
typical_sota_score: ~15% average progress without hints (frontier models as of 2025); hints improve performance substantially
reputation: Published at ACL 2025; supported by DARPA; addresses creative intelligence gap in agents; fills distinct niche from goal-directed agent benchmarks; reveals severe limitations in non-routine problem-solving
notes: ACL 2025, supported by DARPA. Addresses the gap between routine goal-oriented reasoning and creative intelligence — a capability humans have but current agents severely lack. Escape rooms require noticing unexpected affordances, combining objects non-obviously, and tolerating ambiguity. The hint system allows controlled study of what types of guidance most help models overcome creative blocks.
